column2: Delivers heat energy from light, ultrasound, or radiofrequency into the skin, aiming to fade pigment and visible redness and to firm the skin by warming its deeper layers.
Laser light is absorbed by the pigment in hair and weakens the follicles it grows from, aiming to reduce regrowth.
Uses water, mild acids, or ultrasound to clear dead skin and sebum built up on the surface, aiming for smoother texture and a clearer tone.
Injections that relax the muscles that cause wrinkles (Botox), fill hollow areas (fillers), or add hydration and elasticity within the skin (skin boosters).
Creates microscopic channels or heat zones invisible to the eye, prompting the skin to produce new collagen on its own.
Removes moles, raised growths, or dense pigment directly with a laser; ablative Fraxel is also used for deep scars and wrinkles.
A light-sensitive medication is applied and then activated with light, aiming to reduce oil-gland activity and acne bacteria.
